learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.outcome: Shift 0 has X tallest; E reference visible even before commitment
Shift 1 peak W; message remains gibberish
Shift 19 gives peak E and readable MEET ME AT THE OLD BRIDGE message
20 yields peak D and gibberish; 19 restores English
Counts 3 tried shifts, names 19 and text; explains renaming preserves frequencies, E probably disguised, only25 candidate shifts; historical attribution

prediction.reason: Answerable, but E-labelled reference and peak X already cue the answer strongly.

interaction.reason: Shift changes move frequency peak and simultaneously change readability; adjacent wrong contrast reversible.

payoff.reason: Connects observed peak/readability to preserved frequencies and probabilistic E assumption.

clarity.reason: Chart, letter labels and shift controls legible with immediate text feedback.

transfer.reason: Reusable frequency principle stated for Caesar English messages; no new cipher application or failure case.

surprise.reason: Correct prediction confirms that pattern can expose key despite renamed letters.

visualExplanation.reason: Moving peak against E reference carries key-finding mechanism.

playfulness.reason: Reversible wrong/right shifts let text turn between gibberish and English.

practicalValue.reason: Concrete attack on simple substitution cipher.

depth.reason: Single preserved-frequency mechanism plus finite search observation.

complexity.reason: Links alphabet offset, frequency ranking and readability as verification.
complexity.conceptualDemand: balanced: supported chart and alphabet representation changes
complexity.interfaceBurden: low: step buttons and peak alignment shortcut

whyCool: Moving the tallest bar from X to E turns the entire ciphertext into a readable bridge rendezvous, while one further shift destroys readability.
caveat: The E reference strongly cues the prediction and the example does not test a short message where the most common letter differs.
missingEvidence: Phone, keyboard-only, focus, contrast measurement, zoom/reflow and reduced motion untested
screenshots: Inline observed locked and revealed shift19 states; no saved image file
